title: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
seo_title: Principles of Inheritance and Variation Class 12 Biology Worksheet (NCERT Ch 4)
standard_code: Class 12 Biology, Chapter 4: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
standard_text: Heredity and variation: Mendelian inheritance; deviations from Mendelism – incomplete dominance, co-dominance, multiple alleles and inheritance of blood groups, pleiotropy; elementary idea of polygenic inheritance; chromosome theory of inheritance; chromosomes and genes; sex determination – in human being, birds and honey bee; linkage and crossing over; sex linked inheritance – haemophilia, colour blindness; Mendelian disorders in humans – thalassemia; chromosomal disorders in humans; Down's syndrome, Turner's and Klinefelter's syndromes.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 4 Principles of Inheritance and Variation: monohybrid and dihybrid crosses, test crosses, incomplete dominance, blood groups, sex determination, linkage and genetic disorders. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Test cross with the homozygous recessive reveals the genotype.
body_html:
How to think about it

Mendel's pea crosses showed dominance, segregation and independent assortment: a monohybrid F₂ is 3 : 1 (genotypes 1 : 2 : 1) and a dihybrid F₂ is 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. A test cross with the recessive parent gives 1 : 1 if the plant is heterozygous. Some traits show incomplete dominance (pink snapdragons), codominance and multiple alleles (ABO blood groups), pleiotropy or polygenic inheritance.

Genes lie on chromosomes and linked genes tend to be inherited together. Sex is determined by XX–XY in humans, ZW–ZZ in birds and haplodiploidy in honey bees. Disorders may be Mendelian (haemophilia, sickle-cell anaemia, phenylketonuria) or chromosomal (Down's, Turner's, Klinefelter's syndromes).

Example

Tt × Tt, 400 offspring. Dwarf?

¼ × 400

Answer: 100

Example

RrYy × RrYy, 160 seeds. Wrinkled green?

1/16 × 160

Answer: 10

Common mistakes

  • Writing 3 : 1 for genotypes.
  • Thinking blood group O is dominant.
  • Saying the mother decides the sex of a human child.

faq.a: Crossing an organism of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive one; a 1 : 1 result shows it is heterozygous.
Both alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote, as I<sup>A</sup> and I<sup>B</sup> in blood group AB.

items.q: A heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) is test-crossed with a dwarf plant (tt), giving 66 offspring. How many are expected to be dwarf?
items.e: Tt × tt gives 1 tall : 1 dwarf: 33.

items.q: Why are haemophilia and colour blindness more common in males?
c: males have only one X chromosome, so one recessive allele shows its effect
items.e: Females are usually carriers.

items.e: Tt × Tt gives 3 tall : 1 dwarf, so ¾ of 20 = 15.

items.q: What is linkage?
c: the tendency of genes on the same chromosome to be inherited together
items.e: Recombination happens when crossing over separates them.
